notice: RN bank batch 124: Immunity and infection case studies: HIV with Pneumocystis, lupus nephritis, RA biologics with TB and candidemia. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate follow-up.

rationale.correct: Hypoxemia with a CD4 below 200 and diffuse infiltrates suggests Pneumocystis pneumonia.

perOption.r1: Exertional desaturation is typical of Pneumocystis pneumonia.
perOption.r3: Below 200 is AIDS; high opportunistic infection risk.
perOption.r5: Oral candidiasis, a marker of immune failure.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each CD4 count, indicate the infection the client needs prophylaxis against once the count falls below it.

rows.text: CD4 below 100 with positive toxoplasma antibody

columns.text: Mycobacterium avium complex in some guidelines

rationale.correct: CD4 thresholds guide which opportunistic infections to prevent.

perOption.r3:c1: MAC prophylaxis is only for those not starting ART at once.
perOption.r3:c2: MAC prophylaxis is only for those not starting ART at once.
perOption.r3:c3: MAC prophylaxis is only for those not starting ART at once.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The first-line treatment is {{b1}}. Because the PaO2 is below 70 mm Hg, the nurse anticipates {{b2}} to {{b3}}.

options.text: reduce the lung inflammation when organisms die

rationale.correct: TMP-SMX plus steroids for moderate to severe Pneumocystis.

perOption.b2:c: Usually within 2 weeks, not before the infection is treated.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse include during high-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole? Select all that apply.

options.text: Expect a sulfa allergy to be safe because the infection is serious
Stop the steroid when the fever settles on day 2

rationale.correct: Potassium, skin, blood counts and hydration are monitored.

perOption.e: An allergy history changes the drug choice.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: TMP-SMX IV. Prednisone 40 mg twice daily. Oxygen to SpO2 at least 92%. Airborne precautions until TB is excluded.

questions.stem: The client's sister asks the nurse, "Does my brother have AIDS? Nobody will tell me." The client has not given permission to share health information. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tell the sister that the nurse cannot share the client's health information
Ask the client privately what information may be shared and with whom
Offer to support the client if they choose to tell the family
Explain the diagnosis to the sister since she is a close relative
Leave the chart open at the station so the family can read the results

rationale.correct: HIV information is shared only with the client's consent.

perOption.d: HIV status needs specific consent to share.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Day 3
exhibits.body: Sputum: Pneumocystis jirovecii. TB tests negative; airborne precautions stopped.

questions.stem: Two weeks after starting antiretroviral therapy, for each finding or statement, indicate whether it shows improvement or understanding, or needs follow-up.

rows.text: SpO2 96% on room air with walking
"I take my HIV medicines at the same time every day and never skip."
New fever and swollen neck lymph nodes after starting ART
"Once my viral load is undetectable I can stop the pills."
"Undetectable means I can't pass HIV to a partner through sex."
"I'll keep taking the TMP-SMX until my CD4 is above 200 for months."

rationale.correct: Improvement with ART; new inflammation or plans to stop therapy need follow-up.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

exhibits.title: Week 2 of ART
exhibits.body: Viral load falling. Discharged on ART and TMP-SMX.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest the kidneys are involved.

rationale.correct: Protein, casts, rising creatinine and new hypertension mean lupus nephritis.

perOption.r5: A lupus flare sign, but not a kidney sign.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: During high-dose steroids and mycophenolate, which actions should the nurse take to keep the client safe? Select all that apply.

options.text: Teach hand hygiene and avoiding sick contacts
Report a fever even if it is low grade
Give a live zoster vaccine before discharge
Stop prednisone at once if the client feels well

rationale.correct: Infection prevention, glucose checks and no live vaccines on immunosuppression.

perOption.d: Live vaccines are avoided on immunosuppression.

questions.stem: For each finding, select the medicines that likely contributed. Each row may have more than one answer.

rationale.correct: TNF inhibitors reactivate TB; methotrexate harms marrow, liver and mouth.

increasing methotrexate to control joint pain
missing TB screening before the TNF inhibitor

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Hold methotrexate and adalimumab. Rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol. Pyridoxine.

questions.stem: The nurse learns that the TB test before adalimumab was never done. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tell the provider so the client can be informed
Suggest a checklist that blocks biologic orders without a TB result
Write in the chart that the clinic made a mistake
Keep the information private to avoid upsetting the client

rationale.correct: Report, disclose and fix the system.

perOption.e: Clients have a right to know.

columns.text: Oral or vaginal yeast, or step-down

questions.stem: On day 5, cultures still grow Candida and the provider changes to liposomal amphotericin B. Which actions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give a saline bolus before the dose
Mix the drug in 0.9% sodium chloride
Give it as a rapid IV push over 2 minutes to limit vein irritation

rationale.correct: Premedication, saline loading and kidney and electrolyte monitoring.

perOption.d: Amphotericin is mixed in dextrose 5%; saline makes it precipitate.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.body: Line removed day 1. Cultures still positive. Eye exam: no endophthalmitis.

questions.stem: Thirty minutes into the amphotericin infusion, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Slow or pause the infusion and notify the provider
Give meperidine for rigors as prescribed
Increase the rate to finish before the rigors worsen
Mark the client as allergic and never give the drug again

rationale.correct: Rigors and fever during amphotericin are an infusion reaction.

perOption.e: Infusion reactions are not allergy; premedication is adjusted.

exhibits.body: Plan: 14 days after the first negative culture.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 38-year-old client has had 3 weeks of dry cough, fever and breathlessness that is worse on exertion. The client has lost 7 kg and has white plaques in the mouth. The client tested HIV positive 5 years ago but never started treatment. The client's sister is at the bedside.

exhibits.title: Rheumatology clinic
exhibits.body: A 26-year-old client with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) stopped hydroxychloroquine 2 months ago because of cost. The client has painful swollen hands, a facial rash after a beach holiday, ankle swelling and foamy urine.

caseStudies.title: Rheumatoid arthritis biologic therapy with reactivated tuberculosis

exhibits.title: Admission
exhibits.body: A 58-year-old client with rheumatoid arthritis takes methotrexate 20 mg once weekly, folic acid and adalimumab every 2 weeks. The client has had 6 weeks of night sweats, a cough and 4 kg weight loss. The client was born in a country where TB is common. A latent TB test before adalimumab was not found in the chart.

exhibits.title: Surgical ICU
exhibits.body: A 64-year-old client is on day 12 after a bowel resection with total parenteral nutrition through a central line and broad-spectrum antibiotics. New fever and hypotension developed overnight despite the antibiotics.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
